sentences.text: The plaintiff submits that they have filed the present suit in the representative capacity since the common interest of the plaintiffs is to safeguard and O.S. No.1126/2012 protect the valuable property belonging to the Government.
The plaintiffs are the residents of Shampura, Kaval Byrasandra and Kadugondanahalli Villages and now all the villages have developed and they have been given different names .

The plaintiffs submit that the land bearing Survey No. 115 measuring 03 Acres 08 situated at Kadugondanahalli village is the Government Kharab land and the said property is hereinafter referred to as the schedule property.

The plaintiffs submit that as per the index of Lands and Records of Rights maintained by the Revenue Department, the land bearing the Survey Number 115 is shown as "Government Kharab Land" in "Column No. 7 of the Index of Lands" and there are no entries with regard to the possession and enjoyment of the said land in O.S. No.1126/2012 Column No. 2 of the Record of Rights .

Even in the revenue records maintained by the Revenue Department,
the suit land is shown as "Government Kharab Land" in Column No.9 of the RTC and consequently no individual has got any independent right, title, interest or possession over the schedule property.
The plaintiffs submit that for the year 2012 the name of the Bangalore Development Authority is shown in column no. 9 and 12(2) of the RTC as per MR No. 2/1990-91.

The plaintiffs further submit that under the preliminary notification dated 29.05.1978, various lands situated at Shampura Devarjeevanahalli, Kadugondanahalli and Kaval Byrasandra Village including the suit land were acquired by the Bangalore Development Authority, O.S. No.1126/2012 for the purpose of the layout called "Hennur-Bellary Road II Stage"
The plaintiff submit that in spite of the acquisition of the said land, the 2 nd Defendants namely, the Bangalore Development Authority has not taken possession of the schedule property.

Apart from that the BBMP or the BWSSB have not taken any measures to improve the Schedule Property but on the other hand, the defendants 5 to 9 have been putting up constructions over the portion of the schedule property.
The defendant no. 7 is the present Corporator and the defendants 5 and 6 are none other than the relatives of the defendant no. 7.

The defendants 5 to 7 in collusion with each other, have been putting up construction over the schedule property knowing fully well that the schedule O.S. No.1126/2012 property is the "Government Kharab Land" belonging to the Government.
In this regard the defendants 1 to 4 have not taken any steps in stalling the construction activities in order to protect the schedule property being done by the defendants 5 to 7.

Looking into the illegal constructions being put up by the defendants 5 to 7, the defendant nos. 8 and 9 are also making arrangements to put up construction over the portions of the schedule property and in this regard the plaintiff no. 6 has given several representations to the Deputy Commissioner, Police Authorities, Assistant Commissioner and also to the defendants 1 to 3 in order to protect and safeguard the schedule property and in spite of the said representations, the defendants 1 to 4 have Shiva Shankar.V vs Gok Revenue Secretary on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181870402/
6 not taken any action in the O.S. No.1126/2012 matter.

It is averred that the defendants 5 and 6 own their lands adjacent to the schedule property and knowing fully well about the same, the defendants 5 & 6 have encroached upon the portion of the schedule property and have been putting up constructions over the schedule property and likewise the defendants 8 and 9 are also indulged in putting up unlawful constructions over the portion of the schedule property and if the acts of the defendants 5 O.S. No.1126/2012 to 9 and their men are not restrained at the hands of this Hon'ble Court, the plaintiffs who are the public and citizens and also who are the residents of that locality will be put to untold hardship and irreparable loss and injustice.

In this regard, the plaintiffs have also given several representations to the police authorities, the defendants 1 to 4 and their subordinates but no action has been taken by the defendants 1 to 4 and/or by the police authorities and hence, the plaintiffs having no other alternative, have filed the present suit.

3. In the written-statement the defendant No.2 has denied the allegations against the defendant no.2 and sought for a dismissal of the suit.

The defendant No.3 has contended that the suit is not maintainable in law or on facts since the plaintiffs have not issued any statutory notice as required under Section 428 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporation Act, before instituting the suit against this defendant.
Further, it has denied each and every averment of the plaint.
It is further contended that there is no cause of action for the suit and the present suit is false and vexatious.
Hence, the defendant No.3 has prayed to dismiss the suit.

The defendant No.4 has contended that the suit of the plaintiff for the relief of declaration to declare that the suit property is the Government karab land and for the releif of mandatory injunction is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed.

The defendant no.6 in his written statement, has contended that the suit filed by the plaintiffs is not in compliance with u/sec. 80 of Code of Civil Procedure and Section 64 of Bangalore Development Authority Act and Sec.482 Karnataka Municipalities Act.
It is further contended that the suit filed by the plaintiffs in representative capacity has not complied the procedural aspects.
Therefore, the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable on this ground.
It is averred that part of the land has already been utilized by the BBMP & BWSSB for O.S. No.1126/2012 formation of storm water drainage and roads.
Similarly a part of the said land is utilized for construction of a temple.
In addition to that the 3rd respondent has formed a 60 feet road towards North - South and East West directions for the public purpose.
It is further contended that the schedule property has already lost its original character and the suit property has fallen within the limits of Bhruth Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike.
After acquisition of the suit land and adajacent lands new layouts have been formed on either side of the suit property.

The drainage water from the surroundings area ie., Devarajeevanahalli,

The plaintiffs have purposely and deliberately suppressed about the entire suit land being utilized for various purpose.
It is averred that the plaintiffs are all the joint family members and they are in the habit of creating a nuisance in the locality based on the concocted and created documents.

It is further averred that the plaintiffs are in the habit of initiating proceedings before the courts or authorities as they want to show some disputes are pending pertaining to the land in question in the name of public interest.

REASONS 8. ISSUE Nos.1 TO 6 :- It is the specific case of the plaintiffs that the suit schedule property is comprising of the land bearing sy.No.115 measuring 3 acres 8 guntas situated at Kadugondanahalli Village which according to the plaintiffs is a Government karab land as per the index of lands and record of rights maintained by the government.

Kadugondanahalli and Kaval Byrasandra Village for the purpose of formation of Hennur-Bellary Road, II O.S. No.1126/2012 Stage.
The suit property was also shown in the said Notification.
9. It is now the grievance of the plaintiff that inspite of acquisition of land, the 2nd defendant - BDA has not taken possession of the schedule property.

Neither the BBMP nor the BWSSB have taken any measures to improve the schedule property and taking advantage of the same, the defendants No.5 to 9 have put up constructions over the suit schedule property in collusion with each other.

The plaintiffs being the residents of Shamapura have filed the instant suit to protect the valuable property belonging to the Government in a representative capacity and seek appropriate reliefs before this court.

10. In the present case the plaintiffs though have contended that the above suit is instituted in a representative capacity, but not application is filed along with the plaint O.S. No.1126/2012 under Order I Rule 8 C.P.C. requesting the permission of the court to file the suit in a representative capacity.

11. The provisions of Order I Rule 8 C.P.C. reads as under:
8. One person may sue or defend on behalf of all in same interest.
(1) Where there are numerous persons having the same interest in one suit, -

sentences.text: (2) The Court shall, in every case where a permission or direction is given under sub-rule (1), at the plaintiff's expense, give notice of the institution of the suit to all persons so interested either by personal service, or, where, by reason of the number of persons or any other cause, such service is not reasonably practicable, by public advertisement, as the Court in each case may direct.

(5) Where any person suing or defending in any such suit does not proceed with due diligence in the suit or defence, the Court may substitute in his place any other person having the same interest in the suit.

(6) A decree passed in a suit under this rule shall be binding on all persons on whose behalf, or for whose benefit, the suit is instituted, or defended, as the case may be.
12. In order to seek the relief in a representative capacity, the plaintiffs who claimed to be the villagers of Shamapura Village are required to serve notice to all the interested persons through personal service or any public advertisement, as the Court directs.
The entire purpose of Order I Rule 8 is to allow more persons to litigate making the decree of all the representative parties.

In Writ Petition No. 31334 of 2011 , between Puttamma And Nanjundaiah and O.S. No.1126/2012 Ors.
2015(2) AKR 396, High court of Karnataka referring to Kodia Goundar v. Velandi Goundar,

13. The claim of the plaintiffs that the suit land was a government karab land is not disputed by any of the defendants.

The certified copy of the index of lands at Ex.P1, the certified copies of the RTC at Ex.P2 to 4 from 1971-72 till 1988-1989 clearly demonstrate that the suit land was earlier treated as government karab land.

Pursuant to the acquisition notification by the BDA issued under Section 17 (1) and (3) at Ex.P17 dtd 29.5.1978, the name of BDA is reflected in the RTC extracts 1989-1990 till 2010-2011 in terms of Ex.P4 till Ex.P16.

Similarly the documents at Ex.D.34 to D.40 O.S.
No.1126/2012 comprising of the prelimnary notification , final notification, notification under Section 16(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, mahazar report and certificate of handing over of the possession, produced by DW.2 (Authorized Officer of defendant No.2) clearly disclose that the suit schedule property was acquired by the BDA and possession of the said property was taken over by the BDA under Ex.D.40.
14.

It is forthcoming from the materials on record that the plaintiffs themselves have admitted that the suit schedule property comprising of sy.No.115 of Kadugondanahalli was earlier a Government karab land and now acquired by the defendant No.2 - BDA for formation of Hennur-Bellary road,
Stage - II.
Once the plaintiffs have unequivocally and undeniably admitted the acquisition of land by the BDA.
It does not lie in the mouth of the plaintiffs O.S. No.1126/2012 to assert any right over the acquired land much less common right.

15. In this regard it is beneficial to refer the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case of M/s. Lake View Tourism Vs. Chandrakala and Other in CRP.No.252/2024, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka by referring to the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Commissioner, BDA and others Vs. Brijesh Reddy has held that the post issuance of final notification the land vests with the State and the compensation in respect of there to is required to be determined by the LAO and the procedure in this regard is prescribed under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act and any person who has not accepted the award may make a representation to the Deputy Commissioner who thereupon may make a representation under Section 18 of the Act.

or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.

sentences.text: This would necessarily indicate that the persons to whom it is payable being required to be determined by the Reference Court, requiring the Reference Court to decide on a dispute of title or the right between the claimant and the counterclaimants as regards the land that is subject matter of acquisition.

Therefore, the Civil Court has been left with the jurisdiction only to determine any right with regard to recovery of compensation from the person who has received it from the basis of title and not with regard to title / ownership.

Thus, when once the acquisition proceedings are completed, there would be a bar for the Civil Court to decide a suit for declaration of title or cancellation of sale deed as O.S.
No.1126/2012 regards the property which was the subject matter of acquisition.
16. In the above case the plaintiffs after having admitted the acquisition of land have failed to prove as to how the suit schedule property would retain its character as the Government karab land.

Even if it is assumed that the suit land is a Government karab land and , no declaration can be given by the Civil Court as Section 61 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964 exclusively bars the jurisdiction of the Civil Court in respect of the claims with regard to occupation of a waste and vacant land belonging to the Government under Section 61(g)(iv),

wherein it is specifically held that claims against Government in respect of occupation of the waste or vacant land belonging to the Government does not fall exclusively within the jurisdiction of the court and the same O.S.
No.1126/2012 fall within the domain of Revenue Courts which has exclusive jurisdiction over waste or vacant land belonging to the Government.
17 . Rule 21(2)(b) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Rules states that 'B' phut kharab lands refer to those lands which are reserved for public purpose.

It is further pertinent to note that under Section 67 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, all public roads, streets, lanes and paths, bridges,
ditches, dikes and fences, on or beside the same, the bed of the sea, etc, are declared to be the property of the State Government.
Therefore it is evident that the suit land is declared as a government karab land by virtue of Section 67 of the Karnataka Land Reveune Act, 1964.

While under Section 68 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, if the State Government is of the opinion that the whole or any part of O.S. No.1126/2012 any public road, street, lane, or path which is the property of the State Government is not required for the use of the public, the State Government may, by notification, make a declaration that it is proposed that the rights of the public as well as of all persons in or over any such road, street, lane or path, or part thereof, as the case may be, shall be extinguished.

On the publication of such notification, the Deputy Commissioner, shall,
as soon as possible cause public notice of such declaration to be given at convenient places on, or in the vicinity of,such road, street, lane or path, or part thereof, as the case may be.

In terms of the above statutory provision, the State Government may declare any property even comprising of the public road, street, lane, path belonging to the State Government is not required to the use of the public by making a declaration to that effect.

sentences.text: In the above case it is not the case of the plaintiffs that the subject land was used as a public road, street, lane or path prior to the acquisition of the land by the BDA and therefore they are having a pre existing right over it.

It is not the case of the plaintiffs that the suit land which was earlier the government karab land would continue to retain its character as land reserved for the public use in spite of the acquisition of the land.
The plaintiffs admittedly have not specifically pleaded any pre existing right in relation to the usage of the suit land by the plaintiffs or by other villagers .

It is not their case that the suit property was earlier used by them for the purpose of road or as a grazing ground or for any other public purpose and now on account of acquisition of land ,
they have been deprived of the right to use the land for a specific purpose and therefore, a declaration sought by the plaintiff is necessary from this court as the State O.S. No.1126/2012 government has failed to issue any separate notification under Section 68 of the Karntaka Land Revenue Act, 1964 after the acquisition of the land under the Land Acquisition Act.

In W.P.No.13483/2022 between Agricultural Produce Market Committee, Gubbi Taluk, Gubbi and Executive Officer, Talulk Panchayath, Gubbi Taluk the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has categorically held that even if the land is acquired by the Government, a further declaration under Section 68 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act is mandatory to extinguish the rights of the public over the public road.

In the above case it is not the case of the plaintiffs that the suit land was used as a public road by the Villagers of Kadugondanahalli and as such a further declaration is necessary by the Government for acquisition of land for public purpose to extinguish the prexisting rights of the public.
It is further material to note that the plaintiffs have not at all O.S. No.1126/2012 challenged the acquisition of land by the BDA at any point of time.
Once the acquisition proceedings are complete, the property vests with the beneficiary and the existing title over the said property gets divested.
Any dispute regarding the acquisition of the land cannot be entertained by this Court under Section 9 of C.P.C.

The plaintiffs having admitted the Land Acquisition Proceedings with regard to the subject land cannot continue to assert their right on the basis of the previous character of the subject land without indicating any right on the date of filing of the suit.
The representations produced by the plaintiff from Ex.P.18 to P.25 merely disclose that the suit land is a vacant land and it is being unauthorizedly utilized by the defendant Nos.5 to 9.
None of the materials produced by the plaintiff from Ex.P.1 to P.33 prove that the suit schedule property is being used as a public land after the acquisition of land by the BDA.

No O.S. No.1126/2012 records are produced to show that even after acquisition of the land, the suit land has retained its character as a public land by virtue of any Notification or by virtue of Government Order etc.
19.
The documents produced by the plaintiffs pertain to the records which are available prior to the acquisition of land and not after the acquisition of the land.

No doubt the plaintiffs have elicited from the defendant No.6,/ DW.1 that the sy.no.115 is a phutt karab land or Government karab land,
the existence of sy.no.115 on Western boundary of sy.no.116/1, 116/2 and sy.no.24 and 114 and further the existence of the boundaries of Kadugondanahalli, Kavalabyrasandra Villages on the western side of the suit schedule property,but the said admission would not be fruitful to prove that the suit schedule property continues to O.S. No.1126/2012 retain its character as a Government karab land.

As on the date of the suit i.e. on 07.02.2012 the plaintiffs ought to have proved that the suit land had continued to remain as a public land and further demonstrated the plaintiffs have a legal right with respect to the said subject-matter of the property.

Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act 1963 provides that any person entitled to any legal character or to any right as to any property,

sentences.text: The declaratory relief under Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 is in the nature of equitable relief for granting of an already existing right which has been denied by the other party.

In order to obtain the relief of declaration: the plaintiff must establish that (1) the plaintiff is at the time of the suit entitled to any legal character or any right to any property, (2) The defendant has denied or is interested in denying the O.S. No.1126/2012 character or title of the plaintiff, (3) The declaration asked for is a declaration that the plaintiff is entitled to a legal character or to a right to property, (4) The plaintiff is not in a position to claim a further relief from a bare declaration of his title.

The plaintiffs who are asserting their legal right over the subject land have failed to prove their right at the time of suit and further they have utterly failed to prove that the suit land continues to retain its character as a Government karab land after the completion of the acquisition proceedings and in the result the first element of requirement for the grant of declaration under Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 is not fulfilled.

20. It is the contention of the defendant no.2 that the plaint does not disclose the cause of action and this context it is relevant to refer to the judgement of the Apex Court in O.S. No.1126/2012 Colonel Shrawan Kumar Jaipuriyar vs Krishna Nandan Singh in Civil Appeal NO. 6760 OF 2019, the Supreme Court referring to Court in Church of Christ Charitable Trust and Educational Society Represented by its Chairman v. Cause of action requires infringement of the right or breach of an obligation and comprises of all material facts on which the right and claim for breach is founded,
that is, some act done by the defendant to infringe and violate the right or breach an obligation.
For a right to exist, there must be a corelative duty which can be enforced in a law suit.

A O.S.
No.1126/2012 right cannot exist without an enforceable duty.

The pleadings in the above case fail to establish the existence of the legal right and the consequent violation of a statutory right to create an enforceable right in the court of law for non disclosure of the existence of right over the suit property as described in the plaint schedule.
Hence the defendant no.2 has established that the suit does not disclose the cause of action.

21. When once the plaintiffs have failed to prove or make out any cause of action with regard to the suit schedule property in terms of disclosing their legal right over the suit property the assertion of the plaintiffs that the suit land is the Government Kharab land and it belongs to the Government stands vitiated and the issue no.1 is answered in the negative.

The entire purpose of Order I Rule 8 is to allow more persons to litigate making the decree of all the representative parties.
It is well settled that the application seeking the leave of the court to file a suit in a representative capacity is mandatory in order to assert the common rights of the parties.
Therefore, the Civil Court has been left with the jurisdiction only to determine any right with regard to recovery of compensation from the person who has received it from the basis of title and not with regard to title / ownership.
Thus, when once the acquisition proceedings are completed, there would be a bar for the Civil Court to decide a suit for declaration of title or cancellation of sale deed as O.S.
No.1126/2012 regards the property which was the subject matter of acquisition.
Even if it is assumed that the suit land is a Government karab land and , no declaration can be given by the Civil Court as Section 61 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964 exclusively bars the jurisdiction of the Civil Court in respect of the claims with regard to occupation of a waste and vacant land belonging to the Government under Section 61(g)(iv),
While under Section 68 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, if the State Government is of the opinion that the whole or any part of O.S. No.1126/2012 any public road, street, lane, or path which is the property of the State Government is not required for the use of the public, the State Government may, by notification, make a declaration that it is proposed that the rights of the public as well as of all persons in or over any such road, street, lane or path, or part thereof, as the case may be, shall be extinguished.
In terms of the above statutory provision, the State Government may declare any property even comprising of the public road, street, lane, path belonging to the State Government is not required to the use of the public by making a declaration to that effect.

It is not the case of the plaintiffs that the suit land which was earlier the government karab land would continue to retain its character as land reserved for the public use in spite of the acquisition of the land.
The plaintiffs admittedly have not specifically pleaded any pre existing right in relation to the usage of the suit land by the plaintiffs or by other villagers .
It is not their case that the suit property was earlier used by them for the purpose of road or as a grazing ground or for any other public purpose and now on account of acquisition of land ,
they have been deprived of the right to use the land for a specific purpose and therefore, a declaration sought by the plaintiff is necessary from this court as the State O.S. No.1126/2012 government has failed to issue any separate notification under Section 68 of the Karntaka Land Revenue Act, 1964 after the acquisition of the land under the Land Acquisition Act.
Once the acquisition proceedings are complete, the property vests with the beneficiary and the existing title over the said property gets divested.
The plaintiffs having admitted the Land Acquisition Proceedings with regard to the subject land cannot continue to assert their right on the basis of the previous character of the subject land without indicating any right on the date of filing of the suit.
No O.S. No.1126/2012 records are produced to show that even after acquisition of the land, the suit land has retained its character as a public land by virtue of any Notification or by virtue of Government Order etc.
19.
As on the date of the suit i.e. on 07.02.2012 the plaintiffs ought to have proved that the suit land had continued to remain as a public land and further demonstrated the plaintiffs have a legal right with respect to the said subject-matter of the property.
The declaratory relief under Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 is in the nature of equitable relief for granting of an already existing right which has been denied by the other party.
In order to obtain the relief of declaration: the plaintiff must establish that (1) the plaintiff is at the time of the suit entitled to any legal character or any right to any property, (2) The defendant has denied or is interested in denying the O.S. No.1126/2012 character or title of the plaintiff, (3) The declaration asked for is a declaration that the plaintiff is entitled to a legal character or to a right to property, (4) The plaintiff is not in a position to claim a further relief from a bare declaration of his title.
The plaintiffs who are asserting their legal right over the subject land have failed to prove their right at the time of suit and further they have utterly failed to prove that the suit land continues to retain its character as a Government karab land after the completion of the acquisition proceedings and in the result the first element of requirement for the grant of declaration under Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 is not fulfilled.
Cause of action requires infringement of the right or breach of an obligation and comprises of all material facts on which the right and claim for breach is founded,
that is, some act done by the defendant to infringe and violate the right or breach an obligation.
For a right to exist, there must be a corelative duty which can be enforced in a law suit.
A O.S.
No.1126/2012 right cannot exist without an enforceable duty.
Hence the defendant no.2 has established that the suit does not disclose the cause of action.
In the above the case the BBMP has failed to establish by pleading or evidence s that the neglect or the default alleged against the BBMP by the plaintiffs was in respect of the Karnataka Municipal O.S. No.1126/2012 Corporation Act, 1976 and therefore the statutory notice was mandatory.
The defendant - BBMP has not cross examined the witness of the plaintiffs on this aspect or led any independent evidence.
Therefore the defendant no.3 has miserably failed to prove the requirement of compliance of the provisions of Section 482 of the KMC Act.
